title: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Pursuit Game for Locomotor Agility Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2611.33407v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to rapidly changing motion demands while remaining stable and robust. Recent locomotion controllers are typically designed with either a dense reward that is carefully shaped to encourage steps and penalize falling, or by using a reference tracking reward which teaches the controller to follow predetermined motions. Once a behavior that maximizes the reward is discovered, the controller ceases to learn. While generally stable, reference tracking methods focus on motor control separately from motion generation. Self-play has been proven as an effective technique for superhuman performance on several multiagent games like Go, Starcraft, hide-and-seek, and capture-the-flag. We train neural networks to play the game of multiagent tag in a physics simulator to study if new motion generation and control strategies can emerge through sparse feedback and competitive self-play. translated_title: 用于运动敏捷性预训练的对抗性多智能体追捕游戏
translated_abstract: 敏捷的人形机器人运动需要控制器既能适应快速变化的运动需求，又能保持稳定和鲁棒。现有的运动控制器通常采用两种设计方式：一种是精心设计的密集奖励，用于鼓励迈步并惩罚摔倒；另一种是使用参考轨迹跟踪奖励，教控制器跟随预定的动作。一旦发现能够最大化奖励的行为，控制器就会停止学习。参考跟踪方法虽然总体上稳定，但将运动控制与运动生成分离开来处理。自我博弈已被证明是一种有效的技术，可以在围棋、星际争霸、捉迷藏和夺旗等多种多智能体游戏中实现超越人类的性能。我们训练神经网络在物理模拟器中玩多智能体追逐游戏，以研究新的运动生成和控制策略能否通过稀疏反馈和竞争性自我博弈而涌现。
tldr: 该论文提出通过在物理模拟器中让神经网络玩多智能体追逐游戏进行竞争性自我博弈，利用稀疏反馈使新的运动生成与控制策略得以涌现，从而实现人形机器人运动敏捷性的预训练。
